question: What is the primary objective of medical asepsis?

options.C: Reducing the total number of microorganisms

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on lowering microbial loads to prevent transmission, unlike surgical asepsis which aims for complete elimination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: How should a nurse handle an object when its sterile status is uncertain?

options.A: Use the object only for minor dressing changes
options.B: Inspect the packaging for minor dust particles
options.C: Rinse the item with sterile water before use

explanation: A core principle of aseptic technique dictates that any doubt regarding sterility requires immediate rejection of the item. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which clinical procedure requires the strict application of surgical asepsis?

options.A: Performing a routine bed bath for an adult
options.B: Feeding a patient via a nasogastric tube

explanation: Catheterization introduces a conduit directly into the sterile urinary bladder, demanding a completely sterile approach. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the fundamental difference between clean technique and sterile technique?

options.A: Clean technique requires sterile gloves while sterile technique uses examination gloves
options.B: Clean technique reduces microbial load while sterile technique eliminates all microorganisms
options.C: Clean technique is performed only by doctors while sterile technique belongs to nurses
options.D: Clean technique applies to surgery while sterile technique applies to outpatient wards

explanation: Medical asepsis decreases the number of pathogens, whereas surgical asepsis achieves total microbial eradication. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which link in the chain of infection is directly interrupted by performing hand hygiene?
explanation: Washing hands removes transient microorganisms, preventing them from traveling between patients or surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: A contaminated dressing tray acting as a breeding ground for bacteria represents which element of the infection chain?
explanation: A reservoir is any environment where a pathogen can live, grow, and multiply before infecting a host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly preferred over alcohol-based rubs?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material
options.B: Before entering a general medical outpatient ward
options.C: Immediately after checking a patient's blood pressure
options.D: When touching unsoiled patient chart folders

explanation: Visible dirt and certain spore-forming pathogens require physical friction and washing with soap and water to clear effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: A nurse finishes taking vital signs for a patient with intact skin and no visible body fluids. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Put on sterile gloves before touching the next chart
options.B: Rinse hands under cold running water without soap
options.C: Wash hands rigorously with medicated bar soap
options.D: Perform hand hygiene using an alcohol-based rub

explanation: For routine non-soiled patient contact, alcohol-based hand rubs provide rapid and efficient microbial reduction. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which item of personal protective equipment must be removed first when undressing after a procedure?
explanation: Gloves carry the highest concentration of contaminants and are removed first to prevent transferring pathogens to other surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for wearing an N95 respirator instead of a standard surgical mask?

options.A: Providing sterile protection during major abdominal surgery
options.B: Filtering tiny airborne droplet nuclei circulating in the air
options.C: Preventing large fluid splashes from arterial blood spurts
options.D: Shielding the wearer from direct contact with intact skin

explanation: Respirators create a tight seal capable of filtering out microscopic airborne pathogens like tuberculosis bacilli. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: What width defines the unsterile border around the outer edge of a sterile drape?
explanation: Standard protocol dictates that the outer one-inch margin of any sterile field is unsterile due to handling during setup. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why must a nurse never turn their back on an established sterile field?

options.A: Sterile forceps will automatically slide off the edge of the metal table
options.B: Unobserved areas can become accidentally contaminated without the nurse knowing
options.C: Air currents from the back will blow dust particles onto the sterile supplies
options.D: Hospital regulations require continuous visual supervision of all trays

explanation: Maintaining visual contact ensures that any accidental breach of sterility is immediately noticed and corrected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: How should a nurse manage hand hygiene during unexpected water shortages in a clinic?

options.A: Postpone all direct patient care until municipal water supply returns
options.B: Wear examination gloves continuously without changing between tasks
options.C: Wipe hands clean with standard paper towels without applying liquids
options.D: Use stored water systems like tippy-taps or alcohol-based hand rubs

explanation: Alternative water delivery setups and alcohol rubs maintain infection control standards during municipal supply disruptions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct consequence of healthcare-associated infections?

options.B: Decreased overall length of hospital stay

explanation: HAIs invariably prolong hospital stays rather than shortening them, making infection prevention vital. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)
